perspective:
Harold Padilla’s accessible information:

- Harold is a project manager. He knows Arthur Begum as a friend and police officer, and he has previously relied on Arthur for advice and support.
- In the first coffee-shop meeting, Harold feels frustrated and anxious that his project is behind; he believes his team is unmotivated. He tells Arthur his team seems completely unmotivated and he is at his wit’s end. Arthur suggests trying to understand what drives each team member individually and having one-on-one conversations so people feel valued and understood. Harold admits he has focused mostly on goals/deadlines, agrees to try Arthur’s advice, and feels more hopeful.
- Afterward, Harold feels hopeful and relieved and believes Arthur’s advice will help. He proposes one-on-one chats to the team to understand their motivations. Team Member 1 says it could be helpful; Team Member 2 says they are open to it. Harold says he will schedule time with each person.
- Later, Harold notices the team still is not responding well to the new strategies. He feels disappointed and worried about the project’s future. He tells Arthur he tried the suggestions but the team still isn’t responding well. Arthur suggests there may be deeper issues such as personal conflicts, lack of trust, or external stressors, and that Harold may need to dig deeper. Harold says he hadn’t thought of that, plans another round of meetings, and thanks Arthur.
- In one-on-one meetings, Harold is determined and focused; he believes there may be underlying team issues he hasn’t addressed. He asks team members about concerns. Team Member 1 tells him there is tension between a few people that is affecting work. Harold says he will look into resolving the conflicts and asks if there is anything else. Team Member 2 tells him they feel overwhelmed by the workload and stressed, making motivation hard. Harold says he will see about redistributing tasks and that their well-being matters.
- In the final team meeting, Harold feels optimistic and empowered; he believes addressing individual concerns will improve performance. He intends to create a more supportive, open environment through regular feedback sessions and team-building activities. He tells the team he has heard their concerns and will make changes. Team Member 1 says it sounds great and will help; Team Member 2 agrees and says it is good their concerns are being addressed. Harold says he is glad and urges the team to work together, emphasizing their input and well-being.
